chapter: Kid Ory band personnel and repertoire
title: Ory's earlier band and Teddy Buckner joining
summary: Musicians Smith heard with Ory in his college days, and the night Teddy Buckner first joined.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, who was with Ori when you were going out in your college days?

Well, Buster Wilson was on the piano and Ed Garland, Montutti was with him in the minor hall and Bud Scott. I even heard Bud Scott. I don't think I ever heard Mutt Carey but I did hear people like Andrew Blakeney who I thought very highly of and I remember being in a club called the Beverly Cavern in Los Angeles the night that Teddy Buckner first joined the Ori band. Now, Teddy's a fine horn player. No, no question. He really is a good man. He can really get around but he showed up this first time. He had his trumpet. He later converted to cornet for a little softer sound but he had the trumpet that he'd been playing with the Lionel Hampton group and things like that and he was playing a pretty strident kind of horn and it didn't really fit the Ori style exactly and some of us who were sort of loyal Ori followers were bothered a little bit by this. I remember I came up with a very uncomplimentary name for Teddy which I sincerely regret. I called him My God who's that Bill Screamo or something like that because he was really kind of screaming a bit because that was his immediate background but it wasn't long. It wasn't very darn many weeks before Ori did like to rehearse. He didn't for the little two day a week thing but Ori did like to rehearse and keep his bands sharp and drag out some of the more complicated things some of the tunes that had three and four strains of different keys but it wasn't long before Teddy Buckner was just playing a very nice horn and he shifted to cornet for a softer sound and that of course was a relationship that lasted quite a while.
